skill.name: brainstorming
skill.description: Guides collaborative brainstorming before creative or implementation work. It helps clarify intent, compare approaches, validate designs, and document decisions.
skill.summary: Turn early ideas into validated design plans through structured questions and trade-off analysis.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline code around a file path. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 38 uses Markdown backticks around a documentation path template, not Ruby or shell execution. The file contains prompt guidance only and no executable script block.

content.value_statement: Teams often start implementation before goals, constraints, and trade-offs are clear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured brainstorming before design work begins.
actual_capabilities: Reviews current project context before shaping a new idea.
Asks one focused question at a time to refine requirements.
Compares two or three approaches with trade-offs and a recommendation.
Presents design sections in small reviewable chunks.
Covers architecture, components, data flow, errors, and testing.
Directs the assistant to document the validated design plan.
limitations: It does not replace product strategy or user research.
It depends on the user to validate each design section.
It may need repository access to inspect project context.
It is not an implementation skill by itself.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Feature
use_cases.description: Clarify purpose, constraints, and success criteria before choosing an implementation path.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Approaches
use_cases.description: Evaluate several possible designs and select a recommended direction with clear trade-offs.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Design Document
use_cases.description: Turn a validated idea into a structured design covering architecture, data flow, errors, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to help clarify this idea: [describe the idea]. Ask one question at a time before proposing designs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for product and engineering alignment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to plan a feature for [project]. Start by reviewing context, then identify requirements, constraints, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to compare two or three approaches for [goal]. Recommend one option and explain the trade-offs clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Design Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a validated design document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to turn this validated concept into a design spec. Cover architecture, components, data flow, errors, and testing.

output_examples.input: Plan a dashboard export feature for our analytics app.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks focused questions about users, export formats, permissions, and scale before presenting design options.

output_examples.input: Compare ways to add offline support to a mobile app.
output_examples.output: The assistant presents multiple approaches, explains trade-offs, recommends one, and validates each design section with the user.

output_examples.input: Create a design plan after we agree on the approach.
output_examples.output: The assistant drafts a structured plan covering architecture, components, data flow, error handling, and testing responsibilities.

best_practices: Provide project goals, constraints, and known risks before starting.
Answer each clarification question before asking for the next design section.
Validate the recommendation before requesting a written design plan.
anti_patterns: Skipping questions and asking for immediate implementation.
Using the skill when requirements are already fully specified.
Accepting every proposed feature without checking scope or value.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps turn early ideas into clear design plans through questions, options, trade-offs, and validation.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on planning and design before implementation begins.

faq.question: Can it inspect my project?
faq.answer: Yes, when the assistant has repository access, it can review files, documentation, and recent commits.

faq.question: How many questions will it ask?
faq.answer: It asks one question at a time until the purpose, constraints, and success criteria are clear.

faq.question: What kind of output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect design sections with architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing, and trade-offs.

faq.question: Is it useful for nontechnical ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure creative or product ideas, but technical design sections may be less relevant.
